entries.name: Physical isolation barrier
entries.description: Use an inert, non-absorbing barrier such as a gasket, sleeve, washer, insert, sealant, or compatible insulating layer to electrically isolate dissimilar faying surfaces.
restrictions: Use only where the joint is not required to remain electrically conductive.
Barrier material must be inert and non-absorbing.
notes: This is the cleanest galvanic mitigation because it breaks the electron path rather than trying to tolerate it.

entries.name: Seal faying surfaces
entries.description: Seal faying surfaces and exposed joint edges to exclude electrolyte from the couple interface.
environment_constraints: Required for Class 1 through Class 5 and Class 7 faying surface couples.
restrictions: If sealing is not feasible, justification is required by the corrosion control process.
notes: For graphite or CFRP contacts, sealing is mandatory under CPR 40.

entries.name: Wet install fasteners
entries.description: Apply primer or sealant to the fastener and hole interface before installation to exclude electrolyte from the annular gap.
environment_constraints: Applies to fasteners in corrosive environments and graphite-composite contacts.
restrictions: Installation torque behavior and blind-hole pressure effects must be evaluated.
Electrical bonding fasteners follow a different protection path.
notes: Titanium fasteners in graphite composite joints are specifically permitted when wet installed.

entries.name: Barrier coating on the cathodic member
entries.description: Apply a protective coating system to the more noble member to interrupt the galvanic cell and reduce cathodic driving area.
restrictions: Full coverage is needed for circuit-break behavior.
Partial damage or holidays do not eliminate galvanic risk.
notes: Atlas must surface the coat-the-cathode rule whenever a coating mitigation is recommended.

entries.name: Anodize aluminum
entries.description: Anodize aluminum and post-treat with an approved corrosion-resistant finish to increase surface resistance and suppress corrosion rate without claiming a literal new aluminum EMF.
restrictions: Hot water seal should not be used unless authorized by design authority.
Wear, abrasion, erosion, severe corrosion, and fatigue impacts require explicit design authority review.
notes: Frontend should render anodize as a rate modifier, not a box movement.

entries.name: Sacrificial anode cathodic protection
entries.description: Attach a sacrificial zinc, aluminum, or magnesium anode to drive the protected structure cathodic in wet service.
restrictions: Magnesium underwater use is only acceptable as a sacrificial anode.
Selection depends on service environment and structure.
notes: This is a system-level mitigation, not a default hardware finish.

entries.name: Zinc-nickel plating on steel
entries.description: Apply a zinc-nickel metallic coating to carbon or low-alloy steel where a metallic corrosion-protective coating is required.
application_constraints: Most relevant to carbon and low-alloy steels.
restrictions: High-strength steels require hydrogen-embrittlement prevention and bake-out controls.
Supplemental sealant, primer, or paint may still be required.
notes: This entry is included as the preferred modern steel plating option in Phase 1 guidance.

entries.name: Cadmium plating (restricted use)
entries.description: Cadmium remains an available metallic coating in MIL-STD-889D treatment guidance, but NASA restrictions sharply limit where it may be used.
restrictions: Cadmium shall not be used in crew or vacuum environments.
Cadmium-plated tools and hardware shall not be used in manufacture or test of mission-critical spaceflight hardware.
Cadmium can cause liquid-metal or solid-metal embrittlement in titanium.
notes: Atlas must always surface the restriction text for this entry.

entries.name: Impressed current cathodic protection
entries.description: Use an externally powered cathodic protection system only for appropriate ground or fixed structures where continuous monitoring and control are feasible.
application_constraints: Allowed only for launch structures, ground support equipment, or fixed installations.
environment_constraints: Requires conductive wet service and active monitoring.
restrictions: Prohibited for flight hardware and spacecraft structure in Phase 1 product logic.
source_clauses: BoundState Phase 1 product gate from corrosion handoff
notes: This is a product gating rule, not a MIL-STD-889D normative clause.

entries.name: Titanium fasteners for graphite-composite joints
entries.description: Use titanium fasteners in graphite-based composite joints and wet install them with sealant or primer.
restrictions: Still treat the contact as a dissimilar couple and seal it.
Titanium contact with cadmium or zinc is prohibited.
notes: This is the preferred fastener recommendation for CFRP joints in the current handoff.

entries.name: Passivate stainless hardware
entries.description: Passivate stainless steel and precipitation-hardening stainless steel hardware after machining and before service.
application_constraints: Stainless steels and PH stainless steels.
restrictions: Not required where corrosion-resistant steels are to be inorganically coated.
High-hardness martensitic and PH grades also require hydrogen-embrittlement precautions.
notes: Passivation should be surfaced as a base requirement for stainless fasteners, not a substitute for sealing incompatible joints.
